A forgiving loaf for bananas that have gone very brown. One bowl, no mixer.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 very ripe bananas (about 350 g peeled)
* 75 g melted butter, plus a little for the tin
* 100 g light brown sugar
* 1 egg
* 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
* 1 teaspoon baking soda
* A pinch of salt
* 190 g plain flour
* Optional: 60 g chopped walnuts or chocolate chips

== Method ==
# Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Butter a 23 × 13 cm loaf tin and line the base with baking paper.
# Mash the bananas in a large bowl with a fork. Some lumps are fine.
# Stir in the melted butter, then the sugar, egg and vanilla.
# Sprinkle the baking soda and salt over the top and stir. Add the 190 g of flour and fold until just combined. Fold in nuts or chips if using.
# Scrape into the tin and bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil after 40 minutes if the top darkens too fast.
# Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack.

== Tips ==
* The browner the bananas, the sweeter and more fragrant the loaf.
* Frozen bananas work. Thaw them and include the liquid they release.
* It slices better the next day.
